study_identification_part.si_4_title: Linking Personalized Brain Atrophy to Schizophrenia Network and Treatment Response

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Single-center hospital database; 797 healthy subjects and 91 schizophrenia patients; rs-fMRI subgroup of 652 healthy subjects.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data of 797 healthy subjects and 91 schizophrenia patients ... were retrospectively selected from our hospital database."; "resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data were acquired for 652 of the 797 healthy subjects."

answer.SINGLE-SITE healthy adults rs-fMRI subgr: functional connectivity maps for atrophy network mapping

answer.SINGLE-SITE schizophrenia patients (n=91: apply normative model to compute personalized atrophy maps

answer.SINGLE-SITE rTMS trial subgroup (n=52): clinical utility testing with longitudinal symptom changes

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy controls used to build the normative model; rs-fMRI healthy subgroup used for atrophy network mapping; independent healthy and schizophrenia groups used to validate the normative model; rTMS subgroup used for clinical utility testing.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The healthy subjects were used to establish normative reference ranges for cortical thickness as a function of age and sex."; "Each patient's atrophy network was mapped using resting-state functional connectivity MRI from a subgroup of healthy subjects ( n = 652)."; "we additionally collected structural MRI data of an independent healthy group ( n = 60, mean age ± SD = 25.3 ± 7.40, 34 women) ... These 2 validation groups were used to validate the normative model."; "In total 52 of the 91 schizophrenia patients received rTMS in a randomized clinical trial (RCT). Their longitudinal symptom changes were adopted to test the clinical utility of the personalized atrophy map."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Ji2023.pdf.md: Abstract; Ji2023.pdf.md: Results, Paragraph starting "We constructed a normative model..."
